I shot all 14 pages at 400, 1200, 1920 and 3440 px and wrote `report.md`. Every page fails at at least one width: 53 of 56 page × width rows fail. No page scrolls horizontally at any width.

Your page list plus the extra sub-pages gave 14 pages. They are the five levels, then `sessions-and-tasks`, `deputy`, `process-system`, `deputy/roles`, `deputy/review-page`, `session-record`, one transcript session (`session-00324b25`), one record session (`voice-20261020`) and one cloud-voice session.

I opened and read only about 12 of the 56 shots. The console-error and 404 counts are computed by script for every row. The layout failure reasons come from those shots. I applied them to pages built the same way without opening every shot, and the report says so.

Failures, worst first:
- **404s on every deep page:** 60–110 console errors and 200–350 failed requests per page. The missing files are the day and page streams, `page.js`, task logs and `requirements.md`. The year and month pages have 6–12 errors, only at 1920 and 3440. `mastermind-deputy` owns this.
- **Column layout:** the first column is clipped under the sidebar at 1200 and 1920, tab labels are cut ("Sessior"), and the first column is empty at 3440. `mastermind-page` owns this.
- **400 px header:** the tab bar runs to the screen edge and TESTS is unreachable. Chips and detail tables are cut at the right. Nobody owns this yet.
- **Sessions table at 1920:** names are cut off ("Session and task sy…") while the cost column has spare width. Nobody owns this yet.
- **Wrong or empty content:** the `session-e00f55c9` report tab shows only "Cost: not tracked" and a table of dashes. The 2026 and 2026/10 side columns list task folders (`08/12/apps`) instead of sessions. Nobody owns this yet.
- **Timeout:** `session-e00f55c9/sessions-and-tasks/` timed out at 1920 and 3440 on the first run. It loaded when I stopped waiting for the network to go idle, and those two rows come from that second run.

I filed five tasks on this folder: three new ones for the unowned causes, and two marked COVERED (deputy for the 404s, page for the column layout). I logged "show: report.md — 14 pages, 14 fail". I fixed nothing, and I did not commit these files.

I've explained both mysteries and fixed one real misfiling. The deeper fix and the check script are with a builder that hasn't started yet: it's queued behind Servex's agent cap, and the work isn't merged.

**Mystery 1: `eb0fe509` was a false alarm.** It is the id Figma's `create_session` returned on 10-21; the tab then passed it into Figma tool calls. Every line in the transcript belongs to `e00f55c9`, and nothing in the session store is filed under `eb0fe509`.

**Compaction keeps the id.** I confirmed it for this tab and for one SDK agent.

**Mystery 2: the id switch is a deliberate "renewal".** `ai-system-mastermind` is set to restart fresh once its session is a day old or past 100k tokens (its role's `renew: {hours: 24, tokens: 100000}`).
- On 10-24 at 21:32 its context was 130k, so the next wake started a new session (`7c6c8d93`) replacing `2da03974`.
- It renews only while asleep, so no work in flight is cut off. What it loses is the conversation; the new session starts from the readmes and its inbox.
- The two transcripts share no messages, so each session's own cost is counted once.

**One real cost bug.** Servex hands a session every turn its agent id ever ran, 12 sessions' worth for this agent. That makes each new session's per-task split show its predecessors' spend as "untracked". The builder's first step tags each turn with its session.

**StaleClose was already fixed.** Commit `2007ae0fc` (10-22, 20:36) made it treat a tab as alive while its transcript is being written. The bad close was at 00:02 that morning, before the fix. Its test includes the live-tab case and passes 14/14.

**Fixed: three sessions' costs in one folder.** Folders are named by the first 8 characters of the id. Five test sessions from 09-19 had hand-picked ids sharing those characters (`a1c1d1e1-000N-…`), so three of them wrote their cost into `2026/09/19/session-a1c1d1e1/`. A clash now gets a folder named by the full id. The test passes 9/9, and the existing Session, TaskDirs and StaleClose tests still pass. The old mixed folder hasn't been cleaned up; that's listed as an open item.

**Written:** `core/Session/doc/identity.md` covers how folders are named and every way an id can change. It also covers who writes to which record, how cost follows an id, and the context proposal. It's linked from the core/Session and ai readmes. Your idea that only a session may write to its own record is weighed there. My recommendation is to start by stamping every write with the writer's session id: today a tab's writes just say `"by":"agent"`.

**Proposed to `ai-system-mastermind`:**
- Stop the CLI's own compaction from firing mid-turn. It did six times on 10-24.
- Add a timeout so a stuck compaction can't hang an agent.
- Reuse a long-lived role's session for follow-ups on the same topic within about 30 minutes, and start fresh otherwise.

**Still to do:**
- Run the check script (`Server/SessionIdentity.mjs`) on this tab and on the renewed agent, and add a "Session identity" section to the tracking page. That's the builder's job too.
- Review, merge, and complete the task. A fallback check is set for 23:37.

  3. Steps and nudges, about $10

  7. Session costs, about $6

- **Picks from the queue:** nothing does it automatically yet, because the step that would start the top bucket isn't built. Until then the mastermind or deputy opens `/framework/ai/queue/` at the start of each work block. They take the top bucket when `node Server/usage-now.mjs` shows usage on pace and a spawn slot is free.
- **Merge:** the change is merged as `1165a450e` and `node Server/TaskQueue.mjs --check` in the main tree shows 15 queued. I read the page at 1920 and it shows the 15. The 400 shot caught the page still loading, and I did not read 1200 or 3440.
- **Review:** the reviewer found 5 issues; I counted 2 real. I fixed both: the queue now hides a bucket's children, and each bucket's priority line states the real ordering rule. The other 3 were notes with no change needed.
- **YouTube bucket:** it is your own project, so you may want to drop or schedule it.
